title: Ostkaka
hookLine: Ostkaka (pronounced oost-kah-kah), ost meaning "cheese" and kaka meaning "cake" in Swedish, is known as Swedish cheesecake...

items.name: Crushed graham crackers or digestive biscuits

steps.title: Preheat Oven & Prep Your Pan
steps.instructionTemplate: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and line your baking pan with parchment paper, leaving a slight overhang for effortless lifting. Measure out {eu165_cc}, {eu165_sug}, {eu165_eggs}, and {eu165_sour} so everything is ready and at room temperature for a silky, lump-free batter.

steps.title: Press Crust & Beat Cream Cheese Silky
steps.instructionTemplate: Press {eu165_crumb} with {eu165_but} into a parchment-lined springform pan. Beat {eu165_cc} and {eu165_sug} 2 mins until satin smooth.
steps.creatorSecret: Always use room-temp cream cheese so you never have to over-whip (which causes cracks).

steps.title: Add Eggs, Cream & Bake Slowly
steps.instructionTemplate: Fold in {eu165_eggs}, {eu165_sour}, and {eu165_flv}. Bake at 325°F (165°C) for 45 mins until edges set and center gently wobbles. Let Ostkaka cool for 10–15 minutes so the crumb sets cleanly before slicing into 8 portions, then garnish and serve.
steps.criticalTip: Chill at least 4 hours in the fridge before slicing with a warm wiped knife.
steps.creatorSecret: Dip a sharp knife in hot water and wipe dry between every cut for razor-clean cafe slices.

steps.title: Cool Completely, Garnish & Serve
steps.instructionTemplate: Transfer Ostkaka to a wire cooling rack and let it cool for 15–20 minutes so the interior sets cleanly without crumbling. Lift out using the parchment overhang, garnish as desired, and slice into 8 portions.

ugcQuotes.quote: Zero-fluff steps + Cook Mode timer nailed it on the first batch!
